jobs.description: Career Spotlight: Building from the ground up - WalkMe Blog Home » Digital Transformation Career Spotlight: Building from the ground up By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Lirit Tsimerman, VP of Deal Desk (Sales) When I joined WalkMe as Director of the Commercial Desk, I wasn’t looking to just manage a team, I wanted to build something from the ground up. My first months were all about rolling up my sleeves: learning how the desk supported Sales, where the bottlenecks were, and where we could do better. I’ve always believed the best way to lead is to understand the work firsthand, so that’s exactly what I did. Table of Contents hide From vision to reality Redefining revenue operations A culture that trusts you to dream big What keeps me going Looking back From vision to reality Two years in, I started putting my vision into action. We introduced a quoting tool (CPQ), stood up a dedicated Order Management team, and drew a clear line between OM and Deal Desk responsibilities. Together, we mapped the entire Quote-to-Cash process, built cross-departmental collaboration, and created a workflow that finally felt like it worked for Sales instead of against them. As WalkMe grew, so did my role. I led process innovation, supported global operations, and worked to bring different teams around shared goals. Recently, I was promoted to Vice President, something I see not just as recognition of my growth but of the trust WalkMe has shown me throughout this journey. Redefining revenue operations One of the milestones I’m most proud of has been building two high-performing teams, Deal Desk and Order Management, from scratch. Today, they’re not only trusted advisors to Sales but also key collaborators with Legal, Rev Rec, Billing, and Collections. It wasn’t always that way. When I started, Sales was hesitant to approach Deal Desk. Fast forward a few years, and we’ve become their go-to team, even for questions outside our direct scope. That shift, from avoidance to confidence, is one of my proudest achievements. A standout project was creating the Order Management team. By separating its role from Deal Desk, hiring the right people, and designing a seamless handoff, we brought clarity, balance, and focus to our operations. Both teams are thriving today in their own lanes. A culture that trusts you to dream big From day one, I felt empowered to take big swings and make meaningful change. Even when change came with growing pains, I was trusted, heard, and supported. That support extended outside of work too. Over these years, I’ve not only grown professionally but also built a family. WalkMe’s people-first culture and commitment to work-life balance made that possible. What keeps me going The people. The pace. The possibility. Every day brings something new, and that momentum is energizing. We’re always pushing forward, adopting new technologies like AI, optimizing processes, and finding smarter, faster ways to work. One of our values, Act with Empathy, resonates deeply with me. It’s not just a phrase on a wall, it’s how we collaborate, lead, and show up for one another as colleagues and as people. Looking back How would I summarize my WalkMe journey? There is no better place to learn, dream, achieve, and develop. The trust I’ve been given, the freedom to grow, and the amazing people I work with every day make this place special. It’s never boring, we’re always evolving, and that momentum keeps me motivated. jobs.description: Career Spotlight: From law to leadership - WalkMe Blog Home » Digital Transformation Career Spotlight: From law to leadership By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Gil Wiener, DeepUI Solutions Engineering Manager When I joined WalkMe, I was making a big leap, moving from four years in the alternative investment industry with degrees in Business and Law into an entirely new world: tech. I had no background in engineering or software, but after taking a series of relevant courses, I felt ready to shift directions. WalkMe took a chance on me, bringing me on as a DeepUI Solution Engineer, and that opportunity truly changed the trajectory of my career. Table of Contents hide Finding my footing Defining moments A culture that encourages growth Looking ahead Finding my footing In that first role, I focused heavily on log analysis and content performance, helping ensure WalkMe’s product worked seamlessly for our customers. It was all new to me, but I was eager to learn. Over time, I moved into a Team Lead position, and eventually into my current role as Group Manager, where I now lead a global team. As I’ve grown, so has the scope of my work. I’ve gone from tactical execution to strategic leadership. Today, I focus on cross-functional collaboration, mentorship, and driving innovation across our product and internal operations, especially through the integration of Generative AI. Defining moments Stepping into group leadership has been a defining milestone. It has allowed me to scale the team, develop future leaders, and contribute to WalkMe’s broader product strategy in a meaningful way. One project I’m especially proud of was automating a time-consuming, manual process that was slowing us down. What started as a challenge quickly became an opportunity to think bigger. By streamlining workflows and implementing the right tools, we significantly expanded our team’s capacity and freed people to focus on more strategic work. It was a powerful reminder of the impact of zooming out, spotting inefficiencies, and solving creatively. A culture that encourages growth WalkMe has supported my career every step of the way: through technical training, leadership development, mentorship, and most importantly, the freedom to explore and innovate. My managers and senior leaders have consistently encouraged me to take risks, pursue new ideas, and grow into each role with confidence. What’s kept me here for five years? The people. I work alongside incredibly smart, thoughtful, and driven colleagues who challenge and inspire me daily. I also feel truly seen and supported, from peers to executives, and that kind of culture is rare. Looking ahead In the next 5 to 10 years, I see myself stepping further into senior leadership, helping shape long-term strategy and scaling global programs with real impact. I’m especially passionate about mentoring others and embedding AI and automation into how we operate. Not just to move faster, but to work smarter and better. What keeps me motivated every day is the variety. No two days are the same. There are always new challenges, new opportunities, and the chance to grow and make an impact. How would I sum up my WalkMe journey? A dynamic evolution marked by continuous learning, impactful leadership, and a deep commitment to innovation and growth. Want to join Gil and the WalkMe team? jobs.description: Career Spotlight: From the front lines to VP - WalkMe Blog Home » WalkMe Company News Career Spotlight: From the front lines to VP By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Nate Campbell, VP Customer Success Americas When I first discovered WalkMe, it wasn’t through a job board. It was at my previous company, where WalkMe was the only tool that helped us scale. I remember thinking, “This is something special.” At the time, I had only been in Customer Success for two years, and I was actually about to accept another offer when WalkMe reached out. We moved quickly, completing the interview process in just 48 hours. Before I knew it, I had signed the offer, and my WalkMe journey had officially begun. My first role was as a Customer Success Manager, helping customers implement WalkMe and extract real value from the product. Table of Contents hide Climbing, pivoting, and growing Milestones that matter Growth that fuels leadership Why I’ve stayed Looking ahead Climbing, pivoting, and growing From day one, I’ve stayed rooted in Customer Success, but my path hasn’t been a straight line. And I’m grateful for that. After about a year, I became a Team Lead, supporting a growing team of CSMs and WalkMe Builders in our newly launched Raleigh office. That role quickly expanded into leading a team in New York during a time of massive company growth. Back then, we didn’t yet have a formal Professional Services team, so each CS team acted as both CS and PS. That meant I was learning how to lead both relationship-focused and technical individuals. This unique experience that gave me a deeper understanding of how different parts of the business work together. Later, I made the intentional decision to take what I call a “leadership hiatus,” stepping into an Account Manager role to get back into the details and sharpen my skills. That shift helped me reconnect with the product and see our customers in a new way. I had a lot of success there and eventually transitioned back into a Principal CSM role, where I led some of our top accounts and mentored emerging talent. Eventually, I returned to leadership: first managing our Strategic CS team, then AMER West, and today, I’m proud to serve as VP of Customer Success in North America, overseeing both our Customer Success and Customer Solutions teams. Milestones that matter There are many moments I could point to, but for me, it’s not about one milestone. What matters most is being part of building a company we can all be proud of. WalkMe is ever-evolving, ever-changing. That constant momentum can feel chaotic at times, but for the right people, it’s an incredible place to thrive, learn, and make a lasting impact. That said, I’ll never forget the experience of getting to our IPO. The amount of energy, collaboration, and effort it took to reach that moment is hard to describe. A lot of blood, sweat, and tears went into achieving what we did, and I feel lucky to have gone through it with the incredible people who made it happen. Growth that fuels leadership WalkMe has supported my growth in ways that have shaped me as a leader. I’ve had managers who put me in uncomfortable situations that forced me to grow, and I’ve learned to embrace that discomfort as a sign of progress. I’ve also had access to leadership courses, professional coaches, and opportunities that pushed me to expand my skills well beyond being a “WalkMe expert.” That support has shaped not just my career, but who I am as a leader. Why I’ve stayed It comes down to two things: the people and the product. WalkMe is filled with people who work with urgency, care deeply about our success, and genuinely want to win together. That kind of culture is rare. And the product? I’ve seen firsthand how it can drive positive outcomes in infinite ways — across CRMs, HR platforms, eCommerce, and more. Yes, it can be challenging when you’re working with customers on an e-commerce platform, CRM, HRM, and ERP all in the same day. It can take a toll when you’re first getting started. But once you hit your stride and develop your skillset, you become a true jack of all trades. No two days are ever the same, and you’ll never have a boring day. Looking ahead My goal right now is simple: maximize the potential of my team and this company. If we keep focusing on doing that well today, where I end up in 5 to 10 years will take care of itself. More than anything, I want WalkMe to continue growing while remaining a place where people want to stay and grow. Just like I have. How would I summarize my WalkMe journey? A career shaped by learning, built through grit, and defined by the people I’ve been lucky enough to grow with. Want to join Nate and the WalkMe team? jobs.description: Career Spotlight: Building a market, a team, and a vision - WalkMe Blog Home » Digital Transformation Career Spotlight: Building a market, a team, and a vision By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Kazuhisa Takeya, Director of Sales, Japan When I first joined WalkMe, I was part of the Sales team, focused on connecting customers with a product I believed in. Over time, my role evolved in unexpected ways, not only in title but in impact. I became increasingly drawn to building systems, shaping teams, and helping define how we worked as an organization. That growth led to one of the biggest turning points in my career: my promotion to manager. It was a milestone that reflected more than performance. It was about trust. The company saw potential in me and gave me the support and autonomy to lead, solve challenges, and collaborate with global teams. That support shaped who I am today. Table of Contents hide The moment everything clicked Creating the market, together Looking ahead The moment everything clicked One moment I will never forget is closing my first Enterprise License Agreement. That deal was not just about revenue. It was proof that customers in Japan were beginning to understand the value of Digital Adoption Platforms. Being part of that shift and helping to grow awareness in the Japanese market is something I am deeply proud of. It felt like we were doing something bigger than selling software. We were creating understanding around something entirely new. Creating the market, together Why have I stayed at WalkMe for six years? Because I believe we are building the market ourselves. Every day I feel a strong sense of purpose and fulfillment. There is still so much more I want to do, and so much potential ahead. Not only for me, but for the impact we can make on our customers. What makes this possible is WalkMe’s culture of agility and encouragement. Even as a smaller team in Japan, we are empowered to challenge the status quo, take ownership, and get the support we need quickly and flexibly. That mindset has only strengthened my motivation to serve our customers with everything I have. Looking ahead In the next 5 to 10 years, I see myself becoming a true expert in helping customers leverage generative AI. The possibilities are immense, and I’m excited to be part of that transformation. I want to continue growing side by side with my colleagues, who inspire me daily, and keep achieving meaningful success as a team. How would I summarize my WalkMe journey? I played a part in creating the DAP market. And that’s something I’ll always be proud of. Want to join Kazuhisa and the WalkMe team? jobs.description: Career Spotlight: From CSM to strategist and back again - WalkMe Blog Home » WalkMe Company News Career Spotlight: From CSM to strategist and back again By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Elizabeth Good, Senior Strategic Customer Success Manager I joined WalkMe in 2018 as a Customer Success Manager in our San Francisco office, supporting Strategic accounts. At first, I was very much a jack of all trades, managing onboarding, driving adoption, and helping customers build digital adoption strategies. As I grew in the role, I moved into more specialized positions. I became a Digital Adoption Consultant, then joined the Program Architect team, helping enterprise clients scale WalkMe with long-term governance and expansion strategies. I even spent a year in Services before returning to Customer Success, this time as a Senior CSM bringing a full toolbox of cross-functional experience. Table of Contents hide The Moments That Made It Real Support, Culture, and Growth Looking Ahead The Moments That Made It Real One of the earliest “pinch me” moments came just a month into the job, when I was handed a major, household-name account. By November, I had led a two-day onsite that ultimately helped secure a $1.5M+ renewal. That experience taught me I was more capable than I thought, and I’ve carried that confidence into every challenge since. More recently, I was honored to receive the Top CSM award for North America and celebrated the moment at President’s Club in Thailand. That recognition, along with the “Master of Adoption” award, reminded me how far I’ve come and how supported I’ve been along the way. Support, Culture, and Growth WalkMe has supported my growth not just through diverse accounts and projects, but by investing in my development. I’ve benefited from coaching programs, ERG involvement, and leadership development resources like BetterUp, WalkMe’s coaching offering. These experiences helped me build confidence, navigate change, and stay flexible through transitions, an IPO, a pandemic, and an acquisition. What’s kept me here for nearly a decade? A big part of it is the people — smart, kind, motivated teammates who’ve become close friends. I also appreciate WalkMe’s culture of encouraging exploration, where switching roles or departments is seen as a way to grow, not start over. Looking Ahead In the next few years, I hope to grow into a Principal CSM role. I love the variety this work brings, and I’m especially drawn to the human side — figuring out what drives each client and building strategies that spark real engagement. Outside of work, I’m exploring how AI and automation can support both personal and professional projects. From staying organized at work to building open-source tools that blend design and data, I’ve found AI to be a surprisingly empowering way to stretch my skills and curiosity. My goal at WalkMe is simple: leave things better than I found them. Whether that’s a process, a project, or a customer experience, if I can make it smoother and more thoughtful for the next person, that’s a win. “It began, as many adventures do, with mild confusion and a vague sense of direction — and yet somehow resulted in competence, camaraderie, and the occasional award.” Want to join Elizabeth and the WalkMe team? jobs.description: Career Spotlight: From Recruiting Coordinator to HR Specialist - WalkMe Blog Home » Digital Transformation Career Spotlight: From Recruiting Coordinator to HR Specialist By WalkMe Team Updated November 3, 2025 Jenn Whiteman, People Operations Lead When I joined WalkMe in September 2018 as a Recruitment Coordinator, I was supporting five recruiters with everything from scheduling interviews to sourcing candidates and managing the overall candidate experience. It was fast-paced and people-focused, the perfect foundation for a career I’ve been building ever since. After about a year and a half, I transitioned into a full-cycle Recruiter role, managing the hiring process from end to end. Not long after that, a new opportunity opened on the People Business Partner team for an HR Coordinator, and I knew I had to go for it. That role marked the beginning of a new chapter. Since joining the HR Operations team, my role has evolved into that of an HR Specialist, where I support WalkMe employees globally through every stage of their employee lifecycle. Over three years in, the growth hasn’t stopped. Each new challenge has expanded my skills and deepened my impact. Table of Contents hide A project that made a difference Growing with the right people around me Looking Ahead A project that made a difference One of the achievements I’m most proud of is leading the revamp of WalkMe’s Global Onboarding program. Two years ago, I noticed our onboarding processes varied across regions, and key stakeholders weren’t fully aligned. I took the lead in standardizing onboarding globally, introducing structured touchpoints, strengthening the buddy system, and launching live HR-led onboarding sessions. The result was a more cohesive, engaging, and memorable experience for every new hire, and stronger cross-functional collaboration across the company. Growing with the right people around me Throughout my journey, I’ve had the unwavering support of our HR leadership team. They’ve pushed me to try new things, provided mentorship, and opened doors for me to take on meaningful work. I’ve always felt that my growth was a shared goal, and that’s made a real difference. What’s kept me here for over seven years? Opportunity and people. WalkMe has given me space to learn, challenge myself, and grow in directions I never expected. And the team is incredible — curious, driven, and creative. These are the kind of people who inspire you to show up as your best self every day. Looking Ahead Our global HR team continues to grow (it’s tripled in size since I joined), and I’m excited about the new areas of HR I’ll get to explore. There’s still so much to learn, and I’m looking forward to stretching my skill set alongside a team that’s always evolving. It’s been about learning to navigate change with curiosity, staying adaptable, and growing alongside ever-evolving business needs. And I can’t wait to see where the journey goes next.
